title: Turn a 200-email argument into a dated chronology, privately
why: When a dispute starts, someone spends two days reading back through months of emails to work out who said what, and when. The key sentence is usually buried in a reply to a reply.
idea: An AI running on your own computer reads the whole thread and lists every event, request, promise and refusal with its date and the exact words quoted. Nothing leaves the computer, so confidential correspondence stays private.
how: Save the email thread as text or PDF from your mail program, oldest first.
Open it in LM Studio, a free app that runs an AI on your own computer, with a capable model such as Gemma.
Ask for a chronology: date, who, what was asked, promised or refused, with the exact sentence quoted.
Check each line against its quoted sentence and correct anything the AI misread before using it.
need: The thread exported from your mail program
LM Studio and a model of at least 8 to 12 billion parameters on a computer with 16 GB of memory
Time to check the quotes: the AI finds them, a person confirms them
before: Thread: 'RE: RE: RE: Level 3 slab — revised loads', 187 emails, 14-03-2026 to 02-09-2026
after:
21-03-2026  Engineer: revised loads to follow 'by end of next week'
09-04-2026  Contractor: 'still awaiting revised loads, pour on hold'
16-04-2026  Engineer: revised loads issued, rev C
person: A person checks every quoted sentence against the original email, and decides what the chronology means for the dispute.
watch_out: Very long threads exceed what the AI can read at once: split them by month.
The AI can get a date wrong when an email quotes an older one; the quote shows you which.
It reports what was written, not what was meant, so read the important emails yourself.
explain: An AI on our own computer turns the whole email thread into a dated list of who asked for what, with quotes, so we don't spend days reading back.
